edged 0.3% higher overnight Wednesday, after a 2% gain in regular session. The stock is also headed for its best month since May 2025.
Disney Stock Hits Four-Year High As Theme Parks, Streaming Drive Optimism

Walt Disney’s stock broke above the $125 level on Wednesday, reaching an intraday high of $126.28, its highest level in four years, before closing at $125.60. The gains extend a rally following Disney’s better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results earlier this month.

Several factors help optimism around Disney. Its theme parks business continues to grow profits, while its streaming operations are becoming more profitable ahead of Hulu's planned full integration into Disney+ in December.
Disney plans to

more on content in fiscal 2027, with spending expected to reach about $26 billion, up 9% from fiscal 2026. It expects operating income to rise by high-single digits in Entertainment and Experiences and by double digits in Sports.

Morningstar analyst Matthew Dolgin said Disney's parks, resorts and cruise operations remain its biggest strengths, providing room for further expansion. While streaming remains a challenging business, Dolgin added that Disney has made progress in improving the profit of its services.
According to the analyst, Disney’s established content library and intellectual property could help Disney+ remain competitive as the streaming industry undergoes further changes.
Judge Halts FCC's Early License Review Of Disney’s ABC Stations

According to a Bloomberg report, a federal judge temporarily paused the FCC's early license renewal process for eight ABC-owned stations while Disney's lawsuit against the regulator moves forward. The judge said the government cannot use its authority to punish broadcasters for news coverage or opinions it does not like.

Disney and its ABC unit sued the FCC in August, accusing the regulator of targeting the network for political reasons and violating its free-speech rights. Disney argued that the FCC's reviews are an attempt by the Trump administration to retaliate against ABC for its political commentary and reporting.
What Are DIS Retail Traders Saying
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ with a 66% rise in message volume over the past month.
A user

, “Needs to push higher by a few more dollars to break the ceiling. If so, I've been saying we are 148-160 for DOOMSDAY! Do they have a catalyst, yes.... Santa Claus rally, yes.... are they back for good, with this market who knows!”

Another user said, “This 125 area has shown as resistance going back 11 years (2015) kinda crazy. The only other time it went above was when DIS + was announced and then again in the 2021 crazy stock trading, but once it came down business as usual. I'm thinking if we finally break again we could get a runner here in DIS.”
DIS stock has gained 10% year-to-date.
Disney shares hit a four-year high and waded above $125, extending gains after a strong earnings report.
Growth in theme parks and improving streaming profits are supporting optimism.
A federal judge paused the FCC’s license renewals attempt for eight Disney-owned ABC stations.

title: DIS Stock Breaks Above $125 For First Time Since 2022: Disney Retail Bulls Are Talking About A ‘Santa Claus Rally’
